title: Cargo orientation/setup with current-source attribution
acceptance_criteria: Resolved oriented queries and replacement drops preserve collision, authority, ownership, contents and production physics.
Permission-2 cargo/yaw commands provide complete documented setup through existing loaded-frame and transfer services.
Fixture-only progress reports actual names/tick ages with bounded state, honest outcomes, cleanup and a proven native hook.
Fresh full JVM, focused native and full native evidence has actual counts and safe shutdown; genuine failures remain failed.
manual_steps: After technical readiness, use the normal development launch and a disposable world. As a permission-2 operator with a live controlled body and loaded clear space, run /ms14 shuttle_fixture build; retain its ship ID.

Enter through the front airlock using normal movement/jumping. Run /ms14 shuttle_fixture cargo <ship-id> aboard: one five-unit water jug should appear near the body without overwriting hands or carrier inventory.

Examine and pick up the jug using configured controls, then Drop active hand (default Q). Selection/outlines should agree with the oriented physical-profile proxy, and contents should remain five units. The proxy is not the exact mesh.

Run /ms14 shuttle_fixture yaw <ship-id> 0.4 once; repeat query, pickup and drop as the cabin turns. Replacements should use the current actor-frame world basis without loss. This is a rad/s velocity delta, not an angle or pilot control. Do not test high-speed impacts or pitch/roll.

checks.rationale: One full JVM run includes all 16 geometry/profile/orientation cases and six progress-state cases; expected 3314, report actual. Compile every fixture. Single JUnit stage avoids R6 XML self-overwrite. Stop on failure. scope-r9/SUMMARY.md describes current-source attribution; normal submission binds the packet. Gate logs are lead-produced outputs, not pre-run author evidence.
